 Nature and Environment Singapore Patrick Fok 11/05/2026 November 5, 2026 Smoke from Indonesian forest fires is driving demand for air purifiers while threatening billions of dollars in economic losses across Singapore.
 Copy link Advertisement Singapore is facing one of its worst haze episodes in years as smoke from forest fires in Indonesia pushes air pollution to hazardous levels. The transboundary haze has driven up demand for air purifiers, air filters and face masks, while businesses adapt to growing concerns over air quality and public health. Yet the economic impact could be far-reaching.
 Experts warn that disrupted outdoor work, weaker tourism and falling consumer activity may cost Singapore billions of dollars. As debate intensifies over accountability for plantation-linked fires and enforcement of anti-haze laws, the crisis is reigniting questions about  environmental responsibility , climate conditions and Southeast Asia's recurring haze problem.
